calls.price_at_call: DCF fair value $83.50 (stated) vs $55 current (stated), about 52% upside; forward price/sales a fraction of Nebius's (exact figure drops out of captions)
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 2026-10-15; no flip) — both names are ranked a buying opportunity in a close head-to-head call; the name of his final pick drops out of the captions (file ends mid-sentence), so no winner is recorded. High-risk-tolerance investors only.
calls.base_case: Trailing revenue $7.6bn, up from about $1.5bn; analyst estimates $13bn in 2026 rising roughly 3-4x to about $43bn in later years, with a backlog in the billions that needs more data-centre capacity to serve.
calls.bull_case: Demand exceeds supply, likely through 2027, and lease demand/pricing remain strong while capacity is built.
calls.bear_case: Balance sheet is the main concern: over $51bn of debt and little cash versus its spending plans; industry oversupply risk from 2029-2032 after trillions of build-out, with debt-funded assets exposed if pricing falls.

calls.video_title: 3 AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy Before Earnings!
calls.thesis: BUY, first explicit Couch CRWV direction (all prior tracked CRWV entries were UNCERTAIN; no flip) — in this collaboration (byline 'The Motley Fool and 2 more', with Neil) CoreWeave is Couch's own pick for the neocloud market right now: 'that would be my pick.' He stresses the one thing he wants clarity on in earnings is future funding and debt costs.
calls.base_case: CoreWeave sits in SemiAnalysis's platinum tier for its platform, has repeatedly shown it can build AI infrastructure on time and keep GPUs running at a high pace for AI labs, and recently reported 1.5 gigawatts of active power.
calls.bull_case: It is shifting from long AI-lab contracts toward higher-margin enterprise work, has a strong Nvidia partnership, and demand/supply imbalance should last at least 18-24 months on SpaceX's commentary, with pricing still rising.
calls.bear_case: Funding is the open risk: the market fears the interest rates CoreWeave will pay on future debt, and unlike SpaceX it cannot assume sub-one-year paybacks if build-outs slip.

calls.video_title: Why Is CoreWeave Stock Crashing, and is it a Buying Opportunity? | CRWV Stock Analysis
calls.thesis: Upgrade to BUY (stated in video, dated 14 Oct 2026), low conviction: after downgrading earlier this year when the risk/reward turned unattractive, the crash on rising debt-cost fears now makes it a buying opportunity — DCF $81 vs $66. First tracked Parkevtate CRWV call in calls.json — upgrade is vs his own prior downgrade stated in the video, not a tracked flip.
calls.base_case: Revenue scaling fast — $5.1bn (2025) to analyst-est. $12.87bn (2026), $26.3bn (2027, +104%), $42.8bn (2028, +63%) — giving a larger base to service debt; bond yield ~14.5% was already in his cost-of-debt maths, after-tax ~12.5%.
calls.bull_case: Data centres are built against waiting demand; FCF turns positive in 2029 (~$5bn est.) and grows from there.
calls.bear_case: Long-term debt >$51bn (vs ~$10bn Jan 2025), funded almost entirely with debt; est. FCF -$28.5bn (2026), -$32bn (2027), -$22bn (2028); WACC >14%; he calls it one of the riskiest stocks in the market, only for very high risk tolerance.
